text:
Sophia: heads up — CI flake on mteb/rerank job. NDCG numbers look consistently ~0.03 higher for quantized runs when job is parallelized. filing here so we don't lose the trace.
JP: ugh, saw that too. on a hunch I re-ran single-threaded and numbers dropped back. looks like a race in the runner's metric aggregation.
Michael: can you paste logs or a minimal repro?
Sophia: repro attached below, small snippet. run: `pytest tests/evals/test_rerank.py::TestRerank::test_full_suite -n 4` (xdist). logs:```INFO  runner: Starting eval suite mteb_rerank (job=ci-mteb-487)
WARNING metrics: Accumulator reused across tasks
...
RESULT NDCG@10: 0.812
```
Tara: if accumulator reused that's a code smell. we used a global MetricStore for speed, but it wasn't thread-safe.
JP: here's the problematic line I found in runner/metrics.py:```_global_acc = MetricAccumulator()
def get_acc():
    return _global_acc
```This returns same object to all workers under xdist.
Michael: that'd explain higher NDCG (counts merged incorrectly). fix options: make accumulator per-worker, or use contextvars/local storage, or pass collector through task context.
Sophia: I pushed a quick patch to allocate per-eval: `collector = MetricAccumulator()` in run_suite and pass it down. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/402
EvalBot: PR 402 opened by Sophia: label=ci, reviewers=JP,Tara
CI Bot: triggered CI pipeline `ci-mteb-487` for PR 402 — queued
JP: small thought — when switching to per-worker, we should also add an assert in the CI job that runs with xdist to make sure two concurrent suites don't share ids. e.g., assert collector.id == run_id.
Tara: also add a test that runs 6 parallel workers for 10 iterations and checks aggregate equality with sequential run. flake-prone suites should be stress-tested.
Michael: Agree. Also log-level change: turn that warning into an error in test runs so we catch accidental reuse early.
Sophia: repro command (local):```git checkout pr/402
pip install -e .[test]
pytest tests/evals/test_rerank.py::TestRerank::test_full_suite -n 4 -q
```This reproduces on my linux laptop (4 workers).
JP: I ran stress test locally (6 workers, 20 iters) and numbers match sequential now after your patch. thanks.
Tara: can we add a short note to the dashboard docs? the rerank dashboard has an artifact naming convention that assumes stable ids. If metrics were merged incorrectly it polluted historical charts. Add migration note.
Sophia: yep will update docs and add a dashboard migration script to re-run historical aggregates if needed. ticket created: https://redwood-internal/issue/ML-2331
CI Bot: CI job ci-mteb-487 passed on PR 402 — all checks green :white_check_mark:
JP: merging once tests are green and doc note is added. nice catch. :raised_hands:
Michael: follow-up: let's audit other global singletons in eval-harness. I can take that as a short spike.
Sophia: thanks everyone. saving the thread for postmortem notes.
Tara: adding a quick snippet to avoid future regressions — in tests/conftest.py add:```@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def ensure_no_global_singletons():
    for name,obj in globals().items():
        if isinstance(obj, MetricAccumulator):
            pytest.skip("found global accumulator, tests must create per-run")
```Not perfect but catches naive globals.
JP: maybe instead fail hard so nobody skips tests.
Sophia: good point. I'll update to fail.
Michael: OK closing loop — I'll do the audit and open PR for any other globals.
Sophia: thanks — file note: this flake was specific to xdist parallelization + quantized model runs because they already exercise caching paths that hit the metrics merge. worth a short blurb in the release notes.
